mainTopic: An animal born unlike its mother, the prohibition of non-kosher milk, and the sources that kosher milk is permitted
overview: The גמרא first explains the ברייתא: the verse "גמל... טמא הוא" teaches that a non-kosher-looking animal born from a kosher mother is permitted. רבי שמעון disagrees, learning from the double "גמל" that even a camel born from a cow is forbidden. The רבנן use the double "גמל" to forbid camel's milk. רבי שמעון learns the milk from "את", which the רבנן do not expound, as the story of שמעון העמסוני and רבי עקיבא illustrates. The גמרא then explains why a special verse is needed to forbid non-kosher milk at all: kosher milk is itself a surprising permission, so one might have extended it. Next it searches for the source that kosher milk is permitted, rejecting some proofs and accepting others, such as ישי's cheeses and "a land flowing with milk and honey". It also defends expounding the doubled "גמל", even though the list of animals was repeated to add the שסועה. Finally, a ברייתא about a sheep born looking like a goat leads to a question about רבי שמעון's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining the ברייתא: only a camel born from a camel is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא really means. One might think a non-kosher-looking animal born from kosher animals is forbidden, so the verse "גמל... טמא הוא" teaches that only a real camel is טמא. A טמא-looking animal born from a טהור mother is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it is saying: You might have thought, 'Something that comes from animals that chew the cud and have split hooves, do not eat it.' So the verse says: 'The camel... it is impure.' 'It' is impure, but a non-kosher-looking animal born from a kosher animal is not impure. Rather, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is clarifying confusing wording in the ברייתא it just quoted. It explains that the verse comes to permit, not forbid, a strange-looking animal born from a kosher mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "דבר הבא ממעלי הגרה" is the הוה אמינא (the first assumption), and it would have forbidden such an animal. The word "הוא" in "טמא הוא" limits the prohibition to the camel itself, meaning one born from a camel. So the mother decides the status, not how the baby looks.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Introduces a re-reading of a text.
A non-kosher-looking animal born from a kosher mother

steps.confusionAlert: "טמא" and "טהור" here mean forbidden or permitted to eat (non-kosher or kosher). They are not about ritual impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule of our משנה: an animal's kosher status follows its mother.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
A being that comes from those that chew the cud
and from those with split hooves, do not eat it (so one might think)
Therefore the verse states: 'The camel... it is impure'
'It' (a real camel) is impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין טָמֵא הַנּוֹלָד מִן הַטָּהוֹר טָמֵא
phrases.english: but a non-kosher-looking animal born from a kosher one is not impure
rather, it is pure (kosher).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-reads the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that anything born from kosher animals is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: That was only the הוה אמינא. The verse's "הוא" teaches that an animal born from a kosher mother is permitted.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the double 'camel' forbids even a camel born from a cow
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues that "גמל" is written twice in the תורה. One teaches about a camel born from a camel, and the other about a camel born from a cow. Both are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Camel' and 'camel' are written two times. One teaches about a camel born from a female camel, and one teaches about a camel born from a cow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the ruling just given. He holds that a camel-like animal born from a cow is also forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the repeated word is an extra source that adds a case. That case is a camel-looking animal born from a kosher mother. So in his view, the animal's appearance can make it forbidden even when its mother is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Two times (the word appears twice, in ויקרא and in דברים)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
'Camel', 'camel', written two times,
phrases.notes: The camel shows up once in ויקרא 11:4 and again in דברים 14:7.

phrases.english: one for a camel born from a female camel,
and one for a camel born from a cow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view against the ruling of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A camel born from a cow is forbidden, learned from the double "גמל".

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the double "גמל"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן use the second "גמל", since they do not learn רבי שמעון's rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this 'camel', 'camel'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a standard question: if the רבנן reject רבי שמעון's reading, the extra word must teach them something else. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that no word in the תורה is wasted. So the רבנן need their own use for the repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view that disagrees with רבי שמעון)
What do they do with it? (How do they use this verse?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this 'camel', 'camel',
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the רבנן account for the source רבי שמעון just used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the repeated word "גמל".

steps.title: One verse forbids the camel, the other forbids its milk
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, one "גמל" forbids the camel's meat and the other forbids the camel's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is to forbid the animal itself, and one is to forbid its milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the second "גמל" for a different law: the milk of a non-kosher animal is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides now use the repetition. The difference is what it adds: רבי שמעון adds a case (a camel born from a cow), while the רבנן add a product (the milk).

keyTerms.meaning: To forbid the animal itself (its meat)
Its milk (חָלָב, not חֵלֶב, which means forbidden fat)

steps.confusionAlert: "חלבו" here is חָלָב (milk), not חֵלֶב (forbidden fat).

phrases.english: One is to forbid the animal itself,
and one is to forbid its milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לֶאֱסוֹר עַצְמוֹ, וְחַד לֶאֱסוֹר חֲלָבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second "גמל" teaches that camel's milk is forbidden.

steps.title: Where does רבי שמעון learn that camel's milk is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון uses both mentions of "גמל" for his own rule, the גמרא asks where he learns the milk prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, from where does he learn to forbid its milk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. רבי שמעון has used up the extra word, so he needs a different source for the milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that camel's milk is forbidden. The only question is which verse teaches it according to each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֶאֱסוֹר חֲלָבוֹ מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon, from where does he derive the prohibition of its milk?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לֶאֱסוֹר חֲלָבוֹ מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 3, now asking about רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי שמעון's source for forbidding camel's milk.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns the milk from the word "את"
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns the milk prohibition from the extra word "את" in "את הגמל".
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "את הגמל" (the word "את" before "the camel").
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון reads the small word "את" as adding something, here the camel's milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have said just "הגמל". The extra "את" is treated as a ריבוי (an expansion) that includes something connected to the camel, namely its milk.

keyTerms.meaning: A small grammatical word in the Hebrew, which some expound as adding something

phrases.english: He derives it from 'et hagamal' ('the camel').

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5.

steps.title: The רבנן do not expound the word "את"
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן cannot learn the milk from "את", because they do not expound "את" at all. That is why they need the second "גמל".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן do not expound the word "את".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן did not simply use "את" for the milk: in their view, "את" is just normal grammar and teaches nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This exposes the real root of the dispute, which is a method of reading the תורה. רבי שמעון expounds "את", so the second "גמל" is free for the camel born from a cow. The רבנן do not expound "את", so the second "גמל" is needed for the milk.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not expound (they draw no laws from it)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: "את" teaches that the milk is forbidden, and the double "גמל" forbids a camel born from a cow. רבנן: "את" teaches nothing, so the double "גמל" forbids the milk, and a camel born from a cow is permitted.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis do not expound instances of 'et'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Heads off the follow-up question of why the רבנן do not also use "את".
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן do not draw laws from "את", so they need the second "גמל" for the milk.

steps.title: שמעון העמסוני expounded every "את" until he withdrew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought: שמעון העמסוני used to expound every "את" in the תורה. When he reached "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא", he withdrew from this method.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: שמעון העמסוני used to expound every single 'et' in the תורה. When he reached 'You shall fear (et) the Lord your God', he withdrew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that whether to expound "את" is a real, known debate. Here is someone who did expound it and then stopped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא", he could not find anything to add to the fear of ה׳, because nothing may be feared like ה׳. Since one "את" could not be expounded, he gave up the whole method. That matches the רבנן's position.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
A תנא known for expounding every "את"

steps.confusionAlert: He did not stop because he lost interest. He stopped because this one verse seemed impossible to expound. (The same ברייתא goes on, in Step 11, to say that רבי עקיבא later explained it as including תלמידי חכמים.)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Shimon HaAmasoni would expound
each and every 'et' in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְ״אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ תִּירָא״
phrases.english: once he reached 'You shall fear the Lord your God',
he withdrew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the idea, from step 7, that some do not expound "את".
steps.raayaObject: That there is a known approach of not expounding "את".
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about שמעון העמסוני withdrawing from expounding every "את".

steps.title: The students ask about all his earlier teachings
steps.stepSummary: His students ask: if you now withdraw, what happens to all the teachings you derived from "את" until now?
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: רבי, all the 'et's that you expounded, what will become of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The students worry that his withdrawal cancels all his past work. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the method is wrong, then all the laws built on it seem to fall. The students want to know whether his past learning was wasted.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Our teacher,
all the instances of 'et' that you expounded,
what will become of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: רַבִּי, כׇּל ״אֶתִּין״ שֶׁדָּרַשְׁתָּ מָה תְּהֵא עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to his withdrawal in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of all the laws he had already derived from "את".

steps.title: Reward for expounding and reward for withdrawing
steps.stepSummary: שמעון העמסוני answers: just as he received reward for expounding, he receives reward for withdrawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Just as I received reward for the expounding, so I receive reward for the withdrawing.
steps.whatsHappening: He answers his students: both his learning and his honest retraction were מצוות, and both earn reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts that the earlier teachings no longer stand. But he teaches that seeking truth, and stepping back when it requires that, is itself worthy. Retracting for the sake of truth, and for the honor of ה׳, is not a failure.
steps.whatToRemember: The debate over expounding "את" is the root of the dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. שמעון העמסוני's story shows that the method was held and also abandoned, and that honest retraction earns reward.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Just as I received reward for the expounding,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אֲנִי מְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר עַל הַפְּרִישָׁה.
phrases.english: so I receive reward for the withdrawing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁקִּבׇּלְתִּי שָׂכָר עַל הַדְּרִישָׁה, כָּךְ אֲנִי מְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר עַל הַפְּרִישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both expounding and withdrawing for the sake of truth earn reward.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא explains the "את" in fearing God
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the "את" in "את ה׳ אלהיך תירא" stayed unexplained until רבי עקיבא taught that it includes תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until רבי עקיבא came and taught: "You shall fear the Lord your God." The word "את" comes to include Torah scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the story of שמעון העמסוני. Later, רבי עקיבא found a way to explain the "את" that שמעון העמסוני could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון העמסוני stopped expounding "את" because he thought nothing could be added next to fearing God. רבי עקיבא showed that fearing תלמידי חכמים can be included. Still, the point for our sugya is that שמעון העמסוני himself withdrew, and the רבנן follow that approach of not expounding "את".
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי עקיבא's teaching means the רבנן now expound every "את". The sugya only uses this ברייתא to explain why the רבנן do not learn the milk prohibition from "את הגמל".

phrases.english: until Rabbi Akiva came and taught:
"You shall fear the Lord your God"
— to include Torah scholars.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 8 by showing how the troubling "את" was finally explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The "את" in fearing God includes תלמידי חכמים. The ברייתא's background point stands: the רבנן do not expound "את", so they need the second "גמל".

steps.title: Would milk of a non-kosher animal otherwise be permitted?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: since both opinions need a special verse to forbid camel's milk, does that mean that without it such milk would be permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: If so, the רבנן's reason comes from "גמל" "גמל" (written twice), and רבי שמעון's reason comes from "את הגמל". Does that mean that without this, I would say the milk of a non-kosher animal is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. This line sets it up by pointing out a strange implication: we seem to need a verse just to forbid non-kosher milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions work hard to find a source for the milk prohibition. That implies that without the source, milk of a בהמה טמאה would be allowed. The next step shows why that implication is hard to accept.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
If so,
the reason of the Rabbis is from "camel," "camel,"
and Rabbi Shimon's is from "et hagamal,"
then if not for this, I would say
that milk of a non-kosher animal is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusions about the sources ("גמל" "גמל" and "את הגמל") to raise a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a special verse to forbid camel's milk, according to both the רבנן and רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a special verse is needed, it implies that without it the milk would be permitted. But that seems wrong, as the next step shows.

steps.title: A ברייתא already forbids all liquids of impure creatures
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is backed by a ברייתא: the word "הטמאים" forbids the juice, gravy, and sediment of impure creatures, so non-kosher milk should already be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what was taught in a ברייתא? "הטמאים" ("the impure ones") comes to forbid their juice, their gravy, and their sediment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by bringing a source. The source shows that anything coming out of an impure creature is already forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the juice and gravy of a שרץ are forbidden, then milk, which also comes out of an impure animal, should be forbidden for the same reason. So why would we need a separate verse about camel's milk?

keyTerms.meaning: the sediment that settles at the bottom of the pot

phrases.english: What is different from that which is taught:
"the impure ones" — to forbid their juice,
and their gravy, and their sediment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that makes step 12's implication a real difficulty.
steps.raayaObject: That liquids coming from impure creatures are already forbidden, so non-kosher milk needs no special verse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding "הטמאים" to forbid the juice, gravy, and sediment of impure creatures.

steps.title: A verse is needed because milk itself is a novelty
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the special verse is needed. Milk of a kosher animal is already a חידוש, since it comes from spoiled blood. So one might think that the same חידוש permits non-kosher milk too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since milk is a novelty even in a kosher animal (as the Master said, blood spoils and becomes milk), and since it is a novelty, it should be permitted in a non-kosher animal too. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Without a special verse, we might have thought milk is a unique case, different from juice and gravy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milk comes from blood, which is forbidden, yet the Torah permits milk of a kosher animal. That makes milk a חידוש that does not follow normal rules. Because it is a חידוש, one might think it is allowed even from a בהמה טמאה. The ברייתא of "הטמאים" would not be enough, so the special verse teaches that it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: it would have entered your mind to say
a novelty; a law that breaks the normal rules

steps.whatToRemember: Non-kosher milk needs its own verse. Milk is a חידוש, permitted in a kosher animal even though it comes from blood, so one might have wrongly extended that permission to a בהמה טמאה.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does NOT say that milk of a kosher animal is somehow forbidden. It is fully permitted. The point is only that this permission is unusual, and that might have led us to permit non-kosher milk too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This סוגיא is a main source for the הלכה that milk of a non-kosher animal is forbidden.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
for it would have entered your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל דִּבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה נָמֵי חִידּוּשׁ הוּא,
phrases.english: since in a kosher animal too it is a novelty,
as the Master said:
blood becomes spoiled and turns into milk,
and since it is a novelty —
in a non-kosher animal too it should be permitted,
therefore it teaches us (that it is forbidden).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of steps 12-13 by showing why the "הטמאים" source would not cover milk.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity (איצטריך): it shows a reasonable mistaken assumption that the special verse comes to block.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since milk is a חידוש (permitted despite coming from blood), it might be permitted even from a non-kosher animal, unlike juice and gravy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The special verse ("גמל" "גמל" or "את הגמל") teaches that milk of a non-kosher animal is forbidden.

steps.title: The spoiled-blood answer does not fit everyone
steps.stepSummary: The answer from Step 14 depends on the view that milk is spoiled blood. What about the view that a nursing woman's limbs come apart and milk has nothing to do with blood?
steps.simpleTranslation: That answer works well for the one who says the blood spoils and turns into milk. But according to the one who says a nursing woman's limbs come apart and her strength does not return for twenty-four months, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. That answer only works for one opinion about where milk comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said kosher milk is a חידוש because it comes from blood, so we might have permitted non-kosher milk too. But one opinion says a nursing woman stops menstruating because her body is weakened, not because blood becomes milk. For that opinion, milk is not a 'blood' חידוש, so why would we need a verse to forbid non-kosher milk?

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says (it fits one opinion but not the other)
Blood that spoils or becomes cloudy
Her limbs become loose or disjointed (her body is weakened)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'twenty-four months' opinion is not saying milk is dangerous. It only explains why a nursing woman does not menstruate without saying that blood turns into milk.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
the blood spoils and becomes milk,
but according to the one who says
her limbs become disjointed from her
and her strength does not return to her
until twenty-four months,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: He's asking: why would we need a פסוק to forbid milk from a non-kosher animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דָּם נֶעְכָּר וְנַעֲשֶׂה חָלָב, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 because it only fits one opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that kosher milk is a חידוש because it comes from spoiled blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If milk does not come from blood, there is no blood-based חידוש, so the reason for the verse falls away

steps.title: Milk is still a novelty, because it is like a limb from a living animal
steps.stepSummary: Even under the second view the verse is needed. Nothing that comes from a living animal is permitted, yet milk is permitted, so we might have permitted non-kosher milk too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since nothing that comes from a living animal is permitted by the תורה, and this milk is like a limb from a living animal and is still permitted, then even the milk of a non-kosher animal should be permitted. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse is needed for the second opinion as well. It points to a different reason why milk is a חידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally anything taken from a living animal is forbidden, like אבר מן החי. Milk comes from a living animal and is still permitted, so it is a חידוש even without the 'blood' idea. Once milk is a special exception, we might have stretched that exception to non-kosher animals, so the verse is needed to forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken first assumption)
A limb from a living animal, which is forbidden
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: Under both opinions about where milk comes from, kosher milk is a חידוש. That is why the Torah needs a special verse to forbid non-kosher milk.

phrases.english: It was needed,
for it would enter your mind to say:
since there is nothing
that comes from a living animal and the Merciful One permitted it,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי חָלָב כִּי אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי הוּא,
phrases.english: and this milk is like a limb from a living animal,
and yet it is permitted,
therefore even in a non-kosher animal it should be permitted,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the חידוש that works for both opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since kosher milk is a special exception to the rule of אבר מן החי, non-kosher milk would also be permitted
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is needed to teach that non-kosher milk is forbidden

steps.title: What is the source that kosher milk is permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that kosher milk is allowed. It suggests learning it from בשר בחלב, then argues that the proof does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the milk of a kosher animal is permitted? If you say it is because the Torah forbade meat with milk, which implies that milk alone is permitted, we could say instead: milk alone is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit, while meat with milk is forbidden even for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: where do we learn that kosher milk is permitted at all? It offers one possible source and immediately pushes back on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested proof is that if milk alone were forbidden, the Torah would not need to forbid בשר בחלב. The pushback is that the בשר בחלב verse could still teach something new: an איסור הנאה. Milk alone might be forbidden only to eat, so the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
A prohibition on getting any benefit, not just on eating

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not really suggesting that kosher milk is forbidden. It is testing whether this particular proof is strong enough.

phrases.english: And the milk of a kosher animal,
from where do we know it is permitted?
If you say: because the Merciful One forbade 'meat in milk',
which implies that milk alone is permitted,
but say instead: milk alone
is forbidden to eat but permitted for benefit,
while meat in milk is forbidden for benefit as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since kosher milk was assumed to be permitted, the גמרא now asks for the source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that kosher milk is permitted
steps.whyThisMatters: Everything said so far assumed kosher milk is permitted. Now the גמרא looks for the verse that teaches it.

steps.title: Even for רבי שמעון the proof does not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that בשר בחלב is permitted for benefit, so the benefit answer does not work for him. But the verse could still teach that one gets lashes for cooking meat with milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון, who permits benefit from meat and milk, you can still find a reason for the verse: to give lashes for cooking them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the rejection further. Even according to רבי שמעון, the בשר בחלב verse does not prove that milk alone is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the difference cannot be about benefit, since he permits benefit from בשר בחלב. Still, the verse adds something new: a person gets lashes just for cooking meat with milk, which would not apply to milk alone. So the verse has its own purpose, and we still have no proof that milk alone is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find a case for it
Cooking (one is punished for the act of cooking meat with milk)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon,
who permits it for benefit,
you can find a reason for it:
to give lashes for cooking it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rejection of Step 17 to רבי שמעון's view
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from בשר בחלב even according to רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The בשר בחלב verse teaches lashes for cooking, so it does not show that milk alone is permitted

steps.title: A new proof from the law of disqualified sacrificial animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new proof. The תורה forbids the milk of redeemed פסולי המוקדשין, which suggests that the milk of ordinary (חולין) animals is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we can prove it from what the תורה revealed about disqualified sacrificial animals. 'You may slaughter' means you may not shear them. 'Meat' means you may not have their milk. So the milk of ordinary animals must be permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: After the בשר בחלב proof fell apart, the גמרא brings a different proof that kosher milk is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'תזבח ואכלת בשר' lets you slaughter and eat a redeemed פסולי המוקדשין animal. The חכמים learn from it that you may not shear its wool or use its milk. The גמרא reasons that if the תורה needed to forbid milk specifically for these holy animals, then milk from ordinary חולין animals must be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals that became blemished and were redeemed

phrases.english: Rather, since the Merciful One revealed
that regarding disqualified consecrated animals:
phrases.notes: This is about the פסוק in דברים 12:15.

phrases.english: 'You may slaughter', but not shear
'meat', but not milk
this implies that the milk of non-sacred animals is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected בשר בחלב proof with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That milk of kosher חולין animals is permitted to eat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The דרשה on 'תזבח ואכלת בשר' regarding פסולי המוקדשין

steps.title: The difference might only be about benefit, not eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe ordinary milk is forbidden to drink but allowed for benefit, while holy milk is forbidden even for benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could say: the milk of ordinary animals is forbidden to eat but allowed for benefit, while the milk of sacrificial animals is forbidden even for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 19 and shows that it does not prove milk is permitted to drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרשה only shows that holy milk is stricter than ordinary milk. But the stricter level could be about הנאה (benefit). Holy milk would be fully forbidden, and ordinary milk would still be forbidden to drink. So the verse does not prove that ordinary milk may be eaten.

phrases.english: But say: the milk of non-sacred animals is forbidden to eat
but permitted for benefit,
while the milk of sacred animals is forbidden even for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from פסולי המוקדשין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference between holy and ordinary milk could be about אכילה versus הנאה, not about whether one may drink it.

steps.title: A proof from the verse about goats' milk as food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from משלי that calls goats' milk food for your household, which suggests that people drink it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is proven from what is written: 'And there will be goats' milk enough for your food, for the food of your household, and to sustain your maidens.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier proof and tries a new one, a פסוק from משלי (27:27).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes goats' milk as 'your bread' and food for the household. If milk is food, it must be permitted to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it is written

phrases.english: Rather, from what is written:
'And there will be goats' milk enough for your food,
for the food of your household,
and sustenance for your maidens.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That kosher milk may be eaten
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי 27:27, goats' milk described as food

steps.title: Maybe the milk was sold, not drunk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe the פסוק means selling the milk to buy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it means for trade?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from משלי with one short question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Milk for your bread' might mean that you sell the milk and use the money to buy bread. In that case the פסוק says nothing about drinking milk.

phrases.english: But perhaps it is for trade?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Food' could mean income from selling milk, not eating it.

steps.title: A proof from the ten cheeses ישי sent with דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק about the ten cheeses that ישי sent with דוד to the army, which shows that dairy was eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is proven from what is written: 'And these ten cheeses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from שמואל א 17:18, where ישי sends cheeses with דוד for the officer of his brothers' unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheeses sent as provisions to soldiers at war were clearly meant to be eaten, not sold. So dairy, made from milk, was eaten, which shows that kosher milk is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא rejected the proofs from פסולי המוקדשין and from משלי. It now brings the cheeses that דוד brought to the army as evidence that milk products were eaten.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse חָלָב (milk) with חֵלֶב (forbidden fat). The letters are the same, but here it means milk.

phrases.english: Rather, from what is written:
'And these ten cheeses.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That milk and its products are permitted to eat
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 17:18, the ten cheeses brought to the army

steps.title: Maybe the cheese was for selling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that ישי's cheeses may have been sent as goods to sell, not as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the cheese was sent as merchandise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the cheese proof from Step 23. Maybe דוד brought the cheese to the officer so that it could be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as Step 22. There, food for your household was read as money from selling milk. If the cheese was only meant for trade, it proves nothing about eating dairy.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; introduces a possible alternative reading

phrases.english: But perhaps it was for merchandise?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the cheese proof of Step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ten cheeses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cheese could have been for trade rather than for eating

steps.title: Nobody does business in the middle of a war
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends the cheese proof. A war camp is not a place for trade, so the cheese must have been food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it the way of war to do business?! Of course not, so the cheese was for eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brushes off the rejection from Step 24. Soldiers at the front are not running a market, so the cheese was meant to be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trade reading worked in Step 22 because a household can sell its milk. It does not fit a battlefield. The proof from Step 23 therefore stands, and dairy was clearly eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say?! A rhetorical question that rejects a claim

phrases.english: Is it the way of war to engage in commerce?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of Step 24 and restores the cheese proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the alternative reading as unrealistic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cheese could have been trade goods
steps.terutzMaskana: In a war setting, the cheese was food. So eating dairy is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: The cheese of ישי is a proof that holds: dairy was eaten.

steps.title: A land flowing with milk and honey
steps.stepSummary: Another proof: the תורה praises ארץ ישראל for its milk. It would not praise the land with something forbidden to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say a proof from here: 'A land flowing with milk and honey.' If milk were not permitted, would the פסוק praise the land to us with something unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different proof. The תורה praises ארץ ישראל for its milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praise only makes sense if the thing can be enjoyed as food. If milk were forbidden, calling the land flowing with milk would be no praise at all. So milk must be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say; introduces an alternative proof

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it from here:
"A land flowing with milk and honey"
and if it were not permitted,
would the verse praise [the land] to us
with something that is not fit [to eat]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an independent proof that milk is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק praising ארץ ישראל as flowing with milk and honey

steps.title: Come, buy wine and milk
steps.stepSummary: One more proof: ישעיהו invites people to buy and eat wine and milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or say a proof from here: 'Come, buy and eat; come, buy without money and without price, wine and milk.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third option, a פסוק in ישעיהו. It invites people to buy wine and milk and eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא uses milk as a picture of good things to eat. A פסוק would not invite people to buy and enjoy something that is forbidden, so milk must be permitted.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it from here:
"Come, buy, and eat;
and come, buy without money
and without price, wine and milk."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative proof alongside Step 26
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו נה:א: buy and eat wine and milk
steps.whatToRemember: Milk from a kosher animal is permitted. The proofs are ישי's cheese, the praise of ארץ ישראל, and ישעיהו's invitation.

steps.title: Do the other doubled animal names also teach new laws?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the דרשה from the doubled word גמל. It asks: שפן, ארנבת and חזיר are also written twice, so do they also teach these laws?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, 'rock badger, rock badger,' 'hare, hare,' 'pig, pig': do these come to teach these laws too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier argument. There, the word גמל written twice taught an extra law about its milk or about a camel born from a cow. Now it challenges that method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other non-kosher animals are also named twice, once in ויקרא and once in דברים. If a repeated name teaches an extra law, we would need extra laws for each of them, which seems wrong. So maybe the repetition of גמל is not a source for a דרשה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so; pushes a claim to an unacceptable result

steps.confusionAlert: We are no longer talking about whether milk is permitted. The גמרא has jumped back to the earlier דרשה of the doubled word גמל.

phrases.english: But if so,
"rock badger," "rock badger,"
phrases.notes: Named in both ויקרא יא and דברים יד

phrases.english: "hare," "hare,"
"pig," "pig,"
do they come to teach these [laws]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the milk proofs and returns to the earlier דרשה of גמל גמל
steps.kashyaTarget: The דרשה from the repeated word גמל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If repetition teaches an extra law, the other repeated animals should also teach extra laws, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: The animals were repeated for the שסועה and the ראה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains why the non-kosher animals and birds were repeated in דברים. It was in order to add the שסועה and the ראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they come for what a ברייתא teaches: Why were they repeated? With the animals, because of the שסועה; with the birds, because of the ראה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of Step 28. The second listing in דברים has its own purpose: it adds creatures that ויקרא never mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דברים adds the שסועה, an animal with two backs and two spines, to the list of animals. It adds the ראה to the list of birds. So the repetition of שפן, ארנבת and חזיר is fully explained, and they teach no extra laws.

keyTerms.meaning: For that which a ברייתא teaches
An animal with two backs and two spines, added in דברים
A non-kosher bird added in דברים

phrases.english: Rather, [they come] for what is taught [in a baraita]:
Why were they repeated?
With the animals, because of the "shesua";
and with the birds, because of the "ra'a."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the repetition a different purpose, based on a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every repeated animal name might teach an extra law
steps.terutzMaskana: The second list in דברים exists to add the שסועה and the ראה
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: if the repetition is for the שסועה, is the doubled word גמל still free to teach its own דרשה?

steps.title: Then the doubled word for camel should also just be adding the שסועה
steps.stepSummary: If the repeated passage only comes to add the שסועה, then the doubled word גמל was also written for that purpose. So how can anyone learn an extra law from it: רבי שמעון about a camel born from a cow, or the רבנן about camel's milk?
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'camel', 'camel' also came for this purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier דרשות from the doubled word גמל, both the רבנן's and רבי שמעון's. It uses the ברייתא just quoted against them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the whole list of non-kosher animals was repeated in דברים only to add the שסועה. If so, the second גמל is part of that repetition and has already been 'used up'. There is then no extra word left to expound, either for רבי שמעון's camel born from a cow or for the רבנן's milk prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Camel; the word appears twice, and רבי שמעון learns a law from the doubling

phrases.english: 'Camel', 'camel' also
phrases.notes: The word appears in both ויקרא and דברים

phrases.english: came for this purpose!
phrases.notes: 'This' means just to add the שסועה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 29 to attack the original דרשה from the doubled גמל
steps.kashyaTarget: The דרשות from the doubled word גמל: רבי שמעון's (a camel born from a cow) and the רבנן's (camel's milk)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the repetition exists to introduce the שסועה, its words have no extra meaning left to expound.

steps.title: Wherever a repetition can be expounded, we expound it
steps.stepSummary: Even though the passage was repeated for the שסועה, any word in it that can teach something extra is still expounded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever it is possible to expound, we expound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a general rule of reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that a passage was repeated 'only to add one thing' is a fallback. We use it only when nothing else can be learned from the repeated words. Since a lesson can be learned from גמל, we do learn it.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is something to expound

steps.whatToRemember: Saying a passage was repeated for one new detail does not stop us from expounding the other repeated words wherever possible.

phrases.english: Anywhere that there is something to expound,
we expound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A repetition written to add the שסועה cannot teach anything else
steps.terutzMaskana: Any repeated word that can be expounded is expounded, so the doubled גמל still teaches its extra law: for רבי שמעון, a camel born from a cow; for the רבנן, camel's milk

steps.title: A ewe that bore a goat-like animal, or a goat that bore a ewe-like animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the offspring looks like another species, it is exempt from בכורה. If it has some of the mother's signs, it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat, or a goat that gave birth to a kind of ewe, is exempt from בכורה. If the offspring has some of the mother's signs, the mother is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about an animal born looking like a different species. It is setting up a disagreement with רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though sheep and goats are both kosher and both subject to בכורה, the offspring must resemble its own mother to be a בכור. According to this first opinion, even partial resemblance is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Some of the identifying signs (of the mother)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sheep and goats are kosher and subject to בכורה. The exemption comes only from the offspring not resembling its own mother, not from it being a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
a ewe that gave birth to a kind of goat,
and a goat that gave birth to a kind of ewe —
is exempt from the firstborn obligation;
and if it has some of the signs (of its mother) —
the mother is obligated (its offspring counts as a firstborn).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new source dealing with רבי שמעון's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring of another species' appearance is exempt from בכורה, but partial resemblance to the mother makes it obligated

steps.title: רבי שמעון requires the head and most of the body to resemble the mother
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says some signs are not enough. The head and most of the body must look like the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: only once its head and most of its body resemble its mother.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא and sets a stricter requirement for בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first opinion, a few matching signs are enough. רבי שמעון needs real, substantial resemblance: the head plus the majority of the body.

keyTerms.meaning: Its head and the majority of its body

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
not unless its head and most of its body
resemble its mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְאִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The dissenting opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For בכורה, the head and most of the body must resemble the mother

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון need the head and most of the body for eating too?
steps.stepSummary: The question is raised whether רבי שמעון's 'head and most of the body' rule also applies to permission to eat an animal born from a kosher mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: For eating, does רבי שמעון require the head and most of the body, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question of information about רבי שמעון's view regarding eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון forbids a camel-like animal born from a kosher animal (from the doubled גמל). The question is how camel-like it must look to be forbidden. Perhaps permission requires the head and most of the body to resemble the kosher mother, as with בכורה. Or perhaps only some resemblance is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
regarding eating, does Rabbi Shimon require
its head and most of its body, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לַאֲכִילָה, מִי בָּעֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether רבי שמעון's בכורה rule carries over to eating
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון's 'head and most of the body' requirement also governs whether such an animal may be eaten

steps.title: Why eating might be different from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: For בכורה a פסוק demands that both mother and offspring be an ox. For eating, the תורה only forbade a camel, so perhaps the rule is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding בכורה it is written 'But the firstborn of an ox', meaning only when it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox. But regarding eating, it is a camel that the Merciful One said is forbidden, while this one (this passage ends here)...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why there is a question at all, by showing how eating could differ from בכורה. The sentence is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בכורה, the words 'בכור שור' require the offspring to be a real ox like its mother, so the head and most of the body must match. For eating, the prohibition is on a 'camel'. That may mean only a full-looking camel is forbidden, so an animal that is only partly camel-like might be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But the firstborn of an ox' (במדבר יח:יז)
The mother is an ox and its firstborn is an ox

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet an answer. The גמרא is only laying out one side of the doubt, and the sentence continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: Regarding firstborn status, it is written:
'But the firstborn of an ox',
meaning only when it (the mother) is an ox
and its firstborn is an ox.
But regarding eating,
it is a camel that the Merciful One said
is forbidden, but this one...
